title: In an abstract Setoid-flavored ordered ring with 0<=1, the generic numeral builder is monotone
statement: For any AlgS.OrderedRing record R with a witness that le zero one, and naturals m n with m <= n, le (ofNat R m) (ofNat R n) -- the setoid twin of Alg.ofNat_le_ofNat_of_le, using leCongr directly (a first-class field) in place of Eq.rec subst to transport the growing bound.

formal.statement: theorem AlgS.OrderedRing.ofNat_le_ofNat_of_le : ((x0 : AlgS.OrderedRing) -> ((x1 : AlgS.OrderedRing.le x0 (AlgS.OrderedRing.zero x0) (AlgS.OrderedRing.one x0)) -> ((x2 : AxNat) -> ((x3 : AxNat) -> ((x4 : AxNat.le x2 x3) -> AlgS.OrderedRing.le x0 (AlgS.OrderedRing.ofNat x0 x2) (AlgS.OrderedRing.ofNat x0 x3))))))

evidence.supports: AlgS.OrderedRing.ofNat_le_ofNat_of_le admits through the trusted kernel gate. Proved by induction on the Nat.le DERIVATION exactly as Alg.ofNat_le_ofNat_of_le is, with the growing-bound step le_self_add_one built from leCongr directly rather than an Eq.rec subst -- one field application, not a hand-built motive. The zero<=one hypothesis stays explicit and load-bearing (not derivable from OrderedRing's five order laws alone). Instantiated symbolically at both AlgS.Int.orderedRingS and AlgS.Rat.orderedRingS, zero_le_one supplied from le_of_lt applied to the carrier's own zero_lt_one.
evidence.checker_command: out=$(RUST_MIN_STACK=1073741824 cargo test -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib --release -- ofnat_le_ofnat_of_le_s_symbolic_at_int_and_rat --test-threads=1 2>&1) && test "$(printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -cE 'test result: ok\. 1 passed; 0 failed')" -ge 1

notes: Used by linarith::generic's setoid backend (Problem::new_s) to bridge a nonzero certificate residual into the goal's own le relation over an AlgS.OrderedRing, e.g. reached at CReal.orderedRingS by creal_linarith_slack_add_one.
